newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity futures end slightly higher.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity futures end slightly higher.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures ended mostly higher Thursday with upward pressure from forecast cooler temperatures in the U.S. Northwest boosting demand and higher natural gas prices through the West, industry sources said.
"COB (California Oregon Border) prices seemed to move higher in anticipation of some cooler weather in the U.S. Northwest," said one futures broker.
Rising physical natural gas prices were also said to have put some upward pressure on the electricity futures.
October COB ended seven cents higher at $15.44 after trade in a range of $15.20-15.60 per megawatt hour (MWh), while November ended up 20 cents at $16.50 after trading as high as $16.60 per MWh.
Remaining traded COB deferreds settled mostly up to five cents higher.
October Palo Verde settled seven cents higher at $15.80 after trade as high as $15.90, while November settled up 25 cents at $15.15 per MWh.
Remaining COB deferreds closed 10-30 cents higher.
NYMEX said an estimated 198 COB and 157 PV contracts traded Thursday.
-- Chris Reese, New York Power Desk 212-859-1627
